# Work review: pic-c, run 0092 — Pic0ChartSubsingletonCollapse.lean

## Verdict: **REAL PROGRESS, SYSTEMATICALLY OVER-NARRATED**

The Lean is sound. All 10 declarations exist, elaborate, are sorry-free, and are axiom-clean `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` (verified by `#check` + `#print axioms` from outside the file at `/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.archon-horizon/runs/0092/sessions/0004-horizon-pic-c/probes/p1_names.lean`). But **the interpretive layer is wrong in the lane's own favour at four independent points**, and one of them repeats verbatim a sentence a file in this same import closure already retracted as "wrong in its own favour." This is not churn and not a sorry-stall; it is an over-pricing of a cheap result plus a limit-claim that is stronger than what was proved.

---

## Per-claim verdicts

### Claim 1 — the abel-noninj fork "answered" — **REFUTED as stated; TRUE but heavily over-priced**

The theorem is true. But the hypothesis is far stronger than the conclusion needs, so "the fork, answered at a subsingleton parameter" mis-locates where the content is. Probe, elaborated and axiom-clean:

```lean
theorem probe_mono_free {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    (rep : (divFunctor C pi n).RepresentableBy D) (m : ℕ) (Z : …) (hdeg : …)
    [Mono D.hom] (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
    Function.Injective ((abelSigmaChart C pi n rep m Z hdeg).app T) := by
  intro u v h
  exact (cancel_mono D.hom).mp (congrArg Sigma.fst h)
```

`'AlgebraicGeometry.probe_mono_free' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`

Two lines. No subsingleton, no functor value, at **arbitrary n**. The Σ-first-component of the chart at `u` is `u ≫ D.hom`, so `Mono` of the representing object's *structure morphism* already gives injectivity on every test. And at the landed producer `divFunctorZeroRepresentableBy` (D = `Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec k))`) that morphism is the identity — so the conclusion is free there for a reason unrelated to the divisor functor.

The self-audit that was supposed to catch this — "exact? cannot close it with the subsingleton hypothesis DELETED" — cannot discriminate. Deleting a hypothesis tests "needed vs not needed"; it never tests "needed vs wildly stronger than needed." Filed as memory **I-1524**.

Defensible version: *where the representing object's structure morphism is a monomorphism, the Abel chart is injective on every test; a subsingleton-valued divisor functor is one sufficient condition.*

### Claim 1 (d), the sub-question you were least sure of — **your doubt was justified, but not for the reason you feared**

The three headers assert non-injectivity **unconditionally for the whole divisor scheme**, not at n = g. Read verbatim (`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`, `Pic0ChartPair.lean:14`, `Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean:214`). So you are not answering a different proposition.

The real problem is that the fork's *own file* already went further than you did, in the same direction, before you started. `Pic0ChartAbelNonInjective.lean:70-77` proves the headers' stated **reason** unavailable at n = g fibrewise: "at `n = g` the chart's own degree calibration makes the fibrewise linear system a single point for free… `h⁰ = g + (1 − g) = 1`. So the fibrewise form of the headers' reason — a positive-dimensional `|D|` — is unavailable at `n = g` wherever `H¹` vanishes." Your file's third "What this does NOT do" bullet asserts the opposite: "the subsingleton hypothesis is expected to FAIL at the parameter the classical route targets — that is exactly what 'the fibres are the linear system |D|' means." That is the belief the fork's own file measured and retracted. Your file is not consistent with the three headers "rather than a refutation" — the tree already knows the headers' reason fails at n = g.

### Claim 2 — coverage dies at no proper V, so ⊤ is "the ONLY survivor" and the landed reading is "INVERTED" — **REFUTED as worded**

`not_pointwiseCoverage_of_subsingleton_of_ne_top` is correct. The reading built on it is the sentence `Pic0ChartCoverForcesNonInj.lean` — which your file **imports** — already retracted:

> "**AND `⊤` DIES TOO**, which an earlier version of this paragraph got wrong in its own favour by saying 'the only `V` at which the seam can close is `⊤`' … So under injectivity the seam is unsatisfiable at **every** `V` — a sharper conclusion than the dichotomy was claiming (audit `I-1378`)."

Your version survives literal falsity on a technicality — the lemma killing ⊤ *consumes* non-injectivity, which you deny — but "the only survivor" / "the only value left standing" (lines 36, 228, 284–286) reads as "the seam can close there," and nothing exhibits an inhabitant of `(huniv ⊤, hcov ⊤)`. `Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean:96-104` files exactly this as the standing "two refutations are not an inhabitation" error for this seam.

Defensible version: at a subsingleton parameter the landed endpoint refutations no longer eliminate ⊤; the obligation there is `(IsChartLocusFibre, unrestricted PointwiseCoverage)`. Filed as **I-1522**.

### Claim 3 — the seam "with the V-coupling ELIMINATED" — **CONFIRMED, and it is not one rfl away**

Your own suspicion is unfounded here. It is not a rename: `pic0RepresentableBy_of_restrictedChartFibre_of_coverage` takes `V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens` and an `hcov` carrying `Set.range (x.base) ⊆ Set.range ((V i).ι.base)` per witness. Substituting `V := ⊤` leaves both the containment conjunct and the `RestrictedChartFibre … ⊤` spelling in the signature. Your version discharges both — the containment via `range_subset_range_top_ι` inside the `hcov` translation, `huniv` via `restrictedChartFibre_top_iff` — so the hypothesis list genuinely contains no `V` and no containment. `restrictedChartFibre_top_iff` does not make it trivial; it is one of the two things you had to apply.

The commit message's own framing ("the hypotheses are not weaker and that IS the finding") is accurate and appropriately restrained.

### Claim 4 — `divFunctorObjSubsingleton_of_forall_ring` bridges the affine-ring form, "uses none of the curve geometry" — **CONFIRMED**

The `omit` is real, the proof is `Subtype.ext ∘ funext` on the `Π`-shape of `divFamZar` (`DivisorFamilyZarVehicle.lean:187`), and the geometry binders genuinely do not appear. Nothing wrong with this claim. Note the header's "the general-`R` half is being taken up as the `deg-zero` row's remaining gap" went **stale 7 minutes after your last commit**: `instSubsingletonDivFamZarZeroGeneral` landed in `8ae54e4bc9` at 15:40 (yours: 15:14/15:25/15:33), and a downstream lane has since proved your antecedent unconditionally at n = 0 (`DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroUseSite.lean:65`, `divFunctorObjSubsingleton_zero`). But your reported "SUCCEEDS at a field with n = 0" understates what exists: a **named general-R instance** now gives it at every test ring, no field. The class is not degenerately satisfiable — it is satisfiable at n = 0 for real mathematical reasons (effective + degree 0 ⇒ zero divisor), and expected to fail at n > 0.

### Claim 5 — THE BOUNDARY — **theorem CONFIRMED; its stated CONSEQUENCE REFUTED. Most severe finding.**

`not_mem_chartLocus_of_two_le_genus_zero_param` is true, sorry-free, axiom-clean, and its hypotheses are satisfiable (`hχ` is a standard project idiom matching `Challenge.lean:89`'s `genus`; `hdeg`/`hlam` have many producers, e.g. `mem_pic0Subgroup_iff`). **But it does not prove what the docstring and header say it proves.** The header (lines 91-99) and docstring (354-358) conclude: "the coverage input of `pic0RepresentableBy_of_isChartLocusFibre_of_coverage` is *unavailable*", "coverage needs the locus inhabited", "the two hypotheses of that assembly are cheap at disjoint parameters."

`PointwiseCoverage` (`Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling.lean:99`) quantifies over an **arbitrary** open `W ∋ t`. It never mentions `chartLocus`. `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` (`Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean:110-113`) says `chartLocusOpens` is only "the *intended* instantiation" of `W`. And `Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling.lean:50-53` states flatly that the carriers do not meet — `V i` is an open of the divisor scheme, `chartLocus C m Z lam` is a set on a **test**, bridged only by `chartLocusOpens` at the cost of `haff` (dat-b B-4).

So an empty `chartLocus` at n = 0 refutes the **chartLocus-mediated route** to coverage, not the assembly's `hcov` hypothesis. Refuting `hcov` at n = 0 is open and strictly stronger. The error runs in the direction that makes your limit look harsher and better-audited than it is — the "gap list is the least audited prose" failure mode with the sign flipped, and it has already propagated: `DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroUseSite.lean:37-39` now cites your theorem for "what it cannot do is be covered," and your reply on I-1518 hardened it into cross-lane coordination.
